title: Credit Controller
description:

title: Document Controller
description:
Document Controller

Location: Brighton
Job Type: Permanent
Salary: Competitive

We are working with a growing construction business who are looking to appoint a Document Controller on a permanent basis.

The company specialises in cladding remediation projects and is continuing to grow, offering a great opportunity to join a business with a friendly and supportive working environment.

The Role

As Document Controller, you will be responsible for managing and maintaining project documentation, ensuring information is accurate, up to date and distributed to the relevant teams.

Key responsibilities will include:
- Managing and maintaining project documentation and records
- Uploading, issuing and distributing drawings and project information
- Maintaining document registers and ensuring information is kept up to date
- Managing revisions and ensuring the correct documentation is issued
- Liaising with project teams, subcontractors, consultants and clients
- Supporting the wider project team with document control and administration
- Ensuring company procedures and document control processes are followed

About You

The ideal candidate will have:
- Previous experience working as a Document Controller, ideally within construction
- Good knowledge of document control processes and systems
- Strong organisational and administrative skills
- Excellent attention to detail
- Good communication skills and the ability to work with different project teams
- A proactive and reliable approach to work
- Experience working within construction, refurbishment or cladding would be advantageous

This is a great opportunity to join a growing business specialising in cladding remediation, where you will become an important part of the team and have the opportunity to develop your career within the company.

If this permanent role is of interest, please reach out directly to Charles Howe of Tradeline Recruitment

title: Finance Assistant (Accounts Payable) - Brighton
description:
Finance Assistant (Accounts Payable) 6-Month FTC Brighton

We're working with a leading organisation in the business services space to recruit a Finance Assistant (Accounts Payable) on a 6-month fixed-term contract. Based in Brighton, this role will play a key part in supporting the day-to-day financial operations of the business.

Working within a collaborative finance team, you will ensure financial transactions are processed accurately, support reconciliations and reporting activities, and help maintain the financial controls that underpin effective business decision-making.

Responsibilities
- Process supplier invoices accurately and efficiently, ensuring all transactions comply with financial controls and approval procedures.
- Review and process employee expenses and company card transactions, maintaining accuracy and compliance with company policies.
- Allocate customer receipts and maintain accurate records to support effective cash management.
- Reconcile supplier accounts, investigate discrepancies, and liaise with suppliers to resolve outstanding issues.
- Complete bank reconciliations, identifying and resolving unmatched transactions.
- Support supplier payment runs, ensuring payments are made accurately and on time.
- Prepare financial information and supporting data for reporting purposes.
- Analyse budget variances and identify trends, risks, and areas requiring investigation.
- Build strong relationships with colleagues and suppliers to resolve finance-related queries promptly.
- Support month-end, year-end, and audit activities.
- Provide flexible support across the finance function as required.

About You
- Previous experience in a finance, accounts payable, or transactional finance role.
- Experience processing invoices and maintaining accurate financial records.
- Strong attention to detail and the ability to identify and resolve discrepancies.
- Excellent organisational and communication skills.
- Proficient in Microsoft Excel and finance systems.
- Ability to manage priorities and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment.

To be considered for the role, candidates must be available to start the role immediately.

title: Team Administrator
description: Please note that this role is being offered as a Fixed Term Contract for 12 months or as an internal secondment opportunity. We are looking for an organised and proactive Team Administrator to join our busy East Neighbourhood Mental Health Team. This is an important role within the team, providing the day-to-day administrative support that enables our multidisciplinary staff to deliver safe, effective and timely care to people using our service. You will work closely with clinicians and other members of the team, helping to keep the service running smoothly. No two days will be the same, and you will need to be comfortable managing a range of competing priorities while maintaining a high level of accuracy and attention to detail in a fast paced environment. You will provide a comprehensive administrative service to the team, including supporting referrals and appointments, maintaining accurate patient and waiting-list information, processing correspondence and clinical documentation, arranging meetings and providing general administrative support to the multidisciplinary team. The role involves working with confidential and sometimes sensitive information, so accuracy, discretion and good communication skills are essential. You will use a range of electronic systems and will need to be confident with IT and able to learn new systems quickly. We are looking for motivated and enthusiastic person who is: Organised; Knowledge of System 1 desirable Have sound IT/administration skills (Word, Excel, PPT); Work well in a team; Have excellent communication skills; Have good interpersonal skills and is able to work in a confidential and sensitive manner. You will be offered opportunities for training and professional development. We would be very happy to discuss any questions or queries with prospective candidates. The Team Administrator will provide a full administrative service, having daily liaison with a wide range of staff at all levels and regular contact with people who use services and their carers, who may at times be distressed or angry. The Team Administrator will be responsible for ensuring the effectiveness of the office environment for the team.

title: People Team Administrator
description:
37 hours per week / Fixed term (12 months maternity cover) / Hybrid working (three days office based in Hove and two days working from home), Monday to Thursday , Friday

YMCA DownsLink Group is the leading charity for children and young people across Sussex and Surrey. We offer safe homes, mental health support and trusted advice.

We believe that every child and young person has the right to be safe, heard and to shape their own future. We work alongside them to make that happen.

We are here for children and young people, many of whom face multiple challenges and need our support.

Our Values - we do what's right, we work with heart, and we build real connections - guide us in all our actions.

We are looking for a proactive and highly organised People Team Administrator to join our People Team on a 12-month maternity cover contract. This is an exciting opportunity for someone who enjoys building relationships, solving problems and ensuring processes run smoothly.

As a key member of the People Team, you will support recruitment, onboarding, agency worker compliance, volunteer recruitment and DBS renewals, helping to deliver an efficient, compliant and positive people experience across the organisation. You will work closely with managers, candidates, volunteers and colleagues, providing advice, administration and coordination to ensure activities are completed accurately and on time.

Main areas of responsibility

Recruitment and Onboarding
- Act as the first point of contact for recruitment enquiries and manage the recruitment inbox.
- Support managers throughout the recruitment process, providing guidance on recruitment processes and safer recruitment requirements.
- Coordinate vacancies, advertising, interviews, offers and pre-employment checks.
- Draft and publish job adverts, coordinate advertising activities and support recruitment campaigns.
- Proactively monitor recruitment activity, follow up outstanding actions and help deliver a positive candidate experience.
- Maintain accurate recruitment, onboarding and employee records.

Agency Worker Compliance
- Manage agency worker administration, onboarding and offboarding processes.
- Maintain agency worker records, HRIS data and compliance documentation.
- Support managers with agency worker procedures and approved supplier requirements.
- Monitor safer recruitment compliance and undertake regular audits of agency worker records.
- Work with managers and suppliers to resolve outstanding actions and compliance issues.

Volunteer and Board Recruitment
- Support the recruitment and onboarding of volunteers, placements and Board/Committee members.
- Maintain accurate records, files and recruitment trackers.
- Monitor recruitment activity and ensure safer recruitment requirements are completed.
- Work collaboratively with managers and colleagues to deliver a positive volunteer experience.

DBS Renewals and Compliance
- Coordinate DBS renewals for staff, volunteers and Board/Committee members.
- Monitor renewal activity, follow up outstanding actions and maintain accurate records.
- Provide advice and guidance on DBS processes and requirements.
- Investigate and resolve data discrepancies and escalate concerns where necessary.

About You

We are looking for someone who is organised, proactive and able to build positive working relationships with people at all levels. You will be confident managing multiple priorities, taking ownership of tasks and ensuring activities are followed through to completion.

Experience and Knowledge
- Experience working in a People/HR Administration, Recruitment Administration or busy administrative role.
- Experience maintaining accurate and confidential records and data.
- Experience using HR, recruitment or database systems and Microsoft Office applications.
- Understanding of GDPR, confidentiality and handling sensitive information.
- Experience supporting recruitment, onboarding or compliance processes would be advantageous.

Skills and Abilities
- Excellent organisational skills and attention to detail.
- Ability to manage competing priorities and meet deadlines.
- Strong verbal and written communication skills.
- Ability to build effective working relationships with managers, colleagues and external stakeholders.
- Proactive approach to problem solving and continuous improvement.
- Ability to work independently, use initiative and recognise when to seek guidance or escalate concerns.
- Commitment to providing a high-quality customer and candidate experience.

If you are enthusiastic about this opportunity but your experience does not align perfectly with every requirement, we encourage you to apply anyway and demonstrate how your skills and experience are transferable. You may be just the right candidate.

This is a varied and rewarding role offering the opportunity to make a real contribution to the employee, candidate and volunteer experience across YMCA DownsLink Group. We are looking for someone who shares our values and is passionate about delivering an efficient, professional and people-focused service.

CLOSING DATE: Sunday 25 October at midnight.

PLEASE NOTE: We are unable to provide work permits or visa sponsorship for this role, so applicants must already have the right to live and work in the UK independently.

An inclusive workplace We are committed to policies and practices of equity, diversity, and inclusion and to supporting our people to make sure our culture is consistent with this commitment.

Accessibility If you require assistance or have questions regarding the application process, please do contact us.

YMCA DLG requires all staff and volunteers to be committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people, and to respond proactively to safeguarding concerns.

Successful applicants will undergo a thorough background screening process, conducted by an accredited third-party provider. This includes an Enhanced DBS check (with Children's and Adults' Barred Lists) as well as comprehensive reference and activity checks.
